purpose: Choose a source-approved acquisition method before retrieving scholarly or supporting evidence.

method_definitions.official_api: Use the source's documented programmatic API with required authentication, identification, attribution, rate limits, caching, and backoff.
method_definitions.official_bulk_download: Use a source-provided snapshot, FTP, OAI-PMH, dataset export, or other documented bulk interface.
method_definitions.official_feed: Use an official RSS, Atom, JSON Feed, or newsletter archive intended for syndication.
method_definitions.connector: Use an installed first-party or authorized connector that calls the source's supported API.
method_definitions.permitted_web_fetch: Fetch a small number of public pages only after the source's terms and robots policy have been checked and do not prohibit the intended automated access.
method_definitions.permitted_browser_automation: Use Playwright or another browser only for a public page that requires browser rendering, after the source's terms and robots policy have been checked and do not prohibit automation.
method_definitions.document_inspection: Inspect a lawfully accessible or user-provided PDF/HTML document. Respect the document's license and do not bypass access controls.
method_definitions.user_supplied: Use content or identifiers explicitly supplied by the user.
method_definitions.human_observed: Use facts a human explicitly observed in an interactive browser session and recorded for the agent.
method_definitions.local_file_import: Import a file already lawfully present in the workspace.
method_definitions.search_engine_discovery: Use a search engine to discover candidate URLs or snippets; verify substantive claims against the original source when accessible.

global_rules: Prefer an official API, bulk interface, or official feed over HTML access.
Do not downgrade to scraping merely because API credentials, approval, or quota are unavailable.
Before permitted_web_fetch or permitted_browser_automation, check the current terms and robots.txt for the exact host and record the check date and policy URLs.
Browser automation is not a synonym for manual inspection and is never the default fallback.
Do not bypass login, paywall, CAPTCHA, rate limit, robots exclusion, geographic restriction, or other technical access control.
Do not mask identity, rotate IP addresses, or distribute requests to evade limits.
Use the minimum number of requests, cache results, identify the client when requested, honor Retry-After, and apply exponential backoff.
Keep the information source separate from the acquisition method in provenance.
If the policy is unclear or conflicting, use user_supplied or human_observed evidence, or omit the source.
Recheck policy before high-volume, recurring, commercial, or redistributed use.

conditions: Use an API key.
Use per_page up to 100 and cursor pagination for deep result sets.
Monitor meta.cost_usd and rate-limit headers; honor 429 and transient errors.
Use the polite pool by sending a valid mailto parameter and identifying User-Agent when possible.
Cache responses, observe rate and concurrency headers, and back off on 429/403.
For legacy API, RSS, and OAI-PMH, use at most one request every three seconds and one connection at a time.
Cache repeated queries; use OAI-PMH or bulk access for large harvesting.
Metadata may be reused under CC0; full text remains subject to each submission's license.
Use API 2 by default and legacy API v1 only for venues that still require it.
Respect readers, nonreaders, writers, authentication, and venue access controls.
Use public metadata only unless the authenticated user is authorized.
Accept and comply with the current API or dataset license before use.
Use an API key where available, batch endpoints for large jobs, and do not exceed rate limits.
Provide required Semantic Scholar attribution for public outputs.
Confirm that the intended commercial, research, educational, redistribution, and retention use is permitted by the applicable license.
There is no official public bulk API for this workflow.
Respect Google Scholar robots.txt when automated software is involved.
Record observation date because citation counts and version clusters are mutable.
Use Scholar only as a high-recall audit lead and verify records against original sources.
Use NCBI E-utilities URLs and include tool and email parameters.
Without an API key, stay at or below 3 requests per second; with a key, default limit is 10 requests per second.
Schedule very large jobs according to NCBI guidance or use bulk resources.
Use REST, SOAP, OAI, FTP, or documented bulk services.
Check each article's license before reusing or redistributing full text, figures, or supplements.
Prefer the installed GitHub connector or authenticated REST/GraphQL API.
Honor primary and secondary rate limits, Retry-After, and reset headers.
Use public page fetch only for a small number of human-readable pages when API coverage is insufficient.
Use the Reddit Data API only with required registration, OAuth identity, approved use case, attribution, and retention/deletion compliance.
Do not treat absent API approval or credentials as permission to scrape.
For isolated anecdotal evidence without approved API access, accept user-supplied or human-observed permalinks and verify only what is necessary.
Use the official read-only Firebase API for stories, comments, users, and rankings.
Cache item responses and avoid unnecessary recursive traversal even though the official documentation currently states no rate limit.
Prefer Crossref, publisher metadata APIs, citation export, RSS/Atom, or an open-access repository.
For a public page, check current terms and robots.txt before automated fetch.
Use browser automation only when the same public page requires JavaScript and automation is not prohibited.
Inspect only lawfully accessible PDFs or user-provided documents and respect their licenses.
Prefer official APIs, data portals, RSS/Atom, sitemaps, and downloadable reports.
Check current terms and robots.txt before automated web or browser access.
Use browser automation only for public client-rendered pages where it is not prohibited.
Prefer an official RSS/Atom/JSON feed, press-room feed, or documented API when available.
Before fetching an article page, check the current terms and robots.txt for the exact host.
Use Playwright only if the public article requires JavaScript and automation is not prohibited; do not use it merely to imitate a human.
Do not retrieve paywalled text through alternate endpoints or reader-mode bypasses.
Use these sources for reporting and implementation context; verify scientific claims against papers or official documents.
Check official terms, robots.txt, authentication requirements, and available APIs or feeds before automated access.
Use the least invasive method and the minimum number of requests.
If permission is unclear, do not automate; use user-supplied or human-observed evidence.
